overview.definition: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways characterized by variable and recurring symptoms, airflow obstruction, bronchial hyperresponsiveness, and underlying inflammation, manifesting in emergency departments as acute severe bronchospasm.
overview.epidemiology: Affects over 300 million individuals globally, with substantial emergency department admission rates and preventable mortality driven by inadequate maintenance therapy and delayed acute intervention.
overview.pathophysiology: Triggered by allergens, viral infections, or irritants leading to IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation, eosinophilic infiltration, acute bronchoconstriction, mucosal edema, and mucus hypersecretion resulting in elevated airway resistance and dynamic hyperinflation.

authoritative_guidelines.guideline_title: Severe refractory asthma phenotyping, biologic selection, and exacerbation risk reduction
authoritative_guidelines.key_recommendation: Precise biomarker phenotyping (eosinophils, FeNO, IgE) is mandatory for selecting biologic therapies in patients with severe refractory asthma presenting with recurrent emergency exacerbations.

authoritative_guidelines.guideline_title: Clinical practice recommendations on asthma management
authoritative_guidelines.key_recommendation: Emphasizes early combination anti-inflammatory reliever therapy and avoidance of monotherapy SABA to prevent emergency department recidivism.

authoritative_guidelines.guideline_title: Pediatric wheezing and acute asthma emergency management, escalation, and triage
authoritative_guidelines.methodology: WHO Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment (ETAT) Guidelines
authoritative_guidelines.key_recommendation: Rapid triage, immediate administration of inhaled short-acting beta-2 agonists via metered-dose inhaler with spacer, and prompt systemic corticosteroids for pediatric acute wheezing.

authoritative_guidelines.guideline_title: Primary care routine asthma evaluation and maintenance management
authoritative_guidelines.key_recommendation: Routine primary care assessment must incorporate inhaler technique verification and action plan updates to curtail emergency department presentations.

authoritative_guidelines.guideline_title: Clinical practice recommendations on asthma management
authoritative_guidelines.key_recommendation: Standardized criteria for emergency escalation, magnesium sulfate administration, and non-invasive ventilation thresholds in near-fatal asthma.

consensus_points: Immediate administration of high-dose SABA via pMDI with spacer or nebulizer in acute exacerbations.
Systemic corticosteroids must be initiated early (within the first hour) for moderate-to-severe exacerbations.
Avoidance of routine sedatives and anxiolytics due to severe respiratory depression risks.

divergence_points.details: WHO and GINA recommend IV magnesium sulfate reserved strictly for severe refractory exacerbations unresponsive to initial SABA/SAMA therapy, whereas some emergency protocols advocate earlier use in impending arrest.
divergence_points.underlying_reasons: Resource allocation and risk-benefit considerations in overcrowded emergency departments.

red_flags_and_triage: Silent chest (absence of breath sounds indicating severe air trapping)
Cyanosis, altered mental status, or exhaustion
Peak Expiratory Flow Rate (PEFR) < 50% predicted or personal best
Inability to complete sentences in one breath or use of accessory muscles of respiration

diagnostic_strategy.approach: Clinical diagnosis based on acute respiratory distress, wheezing, and variable airflow limitation confirmed by PEFR or spirometry once stabilized; immediate triage via pulse oximetry.
bedside_and_pocus: Point-of-care lung ultrasound to rule out pneumothorax, pneumonia, or acute heart failure
12-lead ECG to evaluate right heart strain or rule out acute coronary syndrome
laboratory_and_biomarkers: Arterial or venous blood gas (ABG/VBG) for severe cases to assess pH, PaCO2, and PaO2
Complete blood count (CBC) to screen for infection or eosinophilia
imaging: Chest X-ray (CXR) indicated only if pneumothorax, pneumonia, or alternative diagnosis is suspected, or in treatment failure.

stepped_management_protocol.title: Immediate Resuscitation & Initial Bronchodilation
stepped_management_protocol.clinical_details: Assess ABCs, apply supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 93-95% (88-92% in chronic hypercapnia), and administer SABA immediately.

medications.dose: 4–10 puffs pMDI with spacer (Adult) / 2–6 puffs (Child) or 2.5–5 mg neb
medications.frequency: Every 20 minutes for the first hour
medications.clinical_notes: Use pMDI with dedicated spacer in preference to nebulizers when possible to ensure superior lung deposition and avoid aerosol dispersion.

medications.frequency: Every 20 minutes for the first hour (moderate-to-severe)
medications.clinical_notes: Add to SABA in moderate-to-severe exacerbations to enhance bronchodilation.

stepped_management_protocol.title: Systemic Anti-Inflammatory Therapy
stepped_management_protocol.clinical_details: Administer systemic corticosteroids without delay in moderate-to-severe exacerbations to reduce airway inflammation and prevent relapse.

medications.clinical_notes: Oral corticosteroids are pharmacologically bioequivalent to IV hydrocortisone and should be preferred unless the patient is unable to swallow or vomiting.

stepped_management_protocol.title: Refractory Exacerbation Escalation
stepped_management_protocol.clinical_details: For severe exacerbations failing initial SABA/SAMA/steroid therapy, administer IV magnesium sulfate.

medications.clinical_notes: Indicated in severe refractory cases with persistent bronchospasm and PEFR < 50% predicted.

landmark_evidence_and_trials.trial_name_or_study: Cochrane Systematic Review on Inhaled Anticholinergics in Acute Asthma
landmark_evidence_and_trials.primary_outcome: Reduction in hospital admissions and improvement in FEV1/PEFR
landmark_evidence_and_trials.clinical_takeaway: Multiple doses of anticholinergics combined with SABA reduce hospital admissions in children and adults with moderate-to-severe acute asthma.

boxed_warnings_and_contraindications: Do NOT use sedatives or anxiolytics in acute asthma exacerbations due to severe risk of respiratory depression.
Do NOT delay systemic corticosteroid administration in moderate-to-severe exacerbations.
monitoring_parameters: Respiratory rate, heart rate, and level of consciousness
Serum potassium levels during high-dose SABA and nebulized therapy
escalation_and_failure_criteria: Physical exhaustion, silent chest, or declining mental status
Failure of PEFR to improve above 50% after 1 hour of aggressive ED treatment
safety_monitoring_and_warnings.special_populations: In pregnancy, maintain aggressive bronchodilator and systemic steroid therapy as hypoxia poses a greater immediate fetal risk than treatment; adjust doses for pediatric weight accordingly.

admission_criteria: Incomplete response to ED treatment after 2-3 hours
PEFR < 40% predicted or personal best after initial treatment
High-risk features (previous near-fatal asthma, recent oral steroid burst, psychiatric comorbidity)
Impending respiratory failure requiring ICU admission
discharge_criteria: PEFR >= 70% of predicted or personal best
Inhaler technique verified and prescribed controller medication supplied with a written asthma action plan
disposition_and_followup.outpatient_followup: Review by primary care physician within 48–72 hours of emergency discharge and specialist referral if severe or recurrent.

evidence_gaps_and_uncertainties: Optimal role of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) vs non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in acute hypercapnic asthma exacerbations.
Exact long-term impact of early biologic initiation during the immediate post-ED window.
guidelines.practical_takeaway: Prompt combination therapy using pMDI with spacer, SABA, ipratropium, and early oral corticosteroids reverses acute bronchospasm rapidly while avoiding unnecessary nebulizer aerosol dispersion and delays.

track_b_scientific_and_epidemiological_e.local_epidemiology_and_cohorts: University hospital registry data from Kasr Al Ainy (Cairo University) and Ain Shams University Hospitals indicate high seasonal emergency department asthma presentations linked to agricultural burning (Black Cloud season) and high urban particulate pollution.
track_b_scientific_and_epidemiological_e.antimicrobial_resistance_and_biomarkers: Unnecessary antibiotic prescribing for acute viral-triggered asthma exacerbations remains a documented target for antimicrobial stewardship initiatives across Egyptian university hospitals.

track_c_real_world_clinical_practice.hospital_and_clinic_patterns: High-volume emergency departments in Cairo and Alexandria rely on rapid triage and aerosol rescue protocols. During equipment shortages, modified spacers are deployed effectively.
resource_limited_workarounds: pMDI with Dedicated Plastic Spacer: In remote district hospitals during jet nebulizer equipment shortages or electrical power outages, 4 to 10 puffs of bronchodilator administered sequentially through a commercial or clean modified plastic bottle spacer is utilized as a pharmacologically bioequivalent alternative to jet nebulization.

Early Oral Corticosteroid Substitution: If IV access line placement is delayed in crowded emergency triage, immediate oral administration of liquid prednisolone or crushed tablets provides bioequivalent systemic anti-inflammatory onset within 1–2 hours.
track_c_real_world_clinical_practice.cultural_and_ramadan_counseling: Dar Al-Ifta and Al-Azhar confirm that pressurized inhalers (pMDI) and emergency non-nutritive nebulizers do NOT break the fast for acute respiratory distress. Patients must not delay emergency care during Ramadan.

guideline_records.guideline_title: WHO consolidated guidelines for the management of common childhood illness: Management of asthma in children and adolescents and bronchiolitis in infants and young children
guideline_records.scope: Pediatric wheezing and acute asthma emergency management, escalation, and triage
guideline_records.abstract: Respiratory illness remains a major contributor to morbidity and mortality among children worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income settings where access to timely diagnosis and treatment may be limited. This document presents consolidated World Health Organization guidelines addressing the management of asthma in children and adolescents and bronchiolitis in infants and young children, two of the most common causes of paediatric respiratory illness and wheezing presentations . It outlines evidence-based recommendations for both acute and long-term management, including pharmacological therapies, supportive care and criteria for clinical decision-making across different levels of the health system. The guideline is informed by systematically formulated clinical questions using the PICO framework and draws on evidence synthesized through systematic reviews, assessed with the GRADE approach and deliberated by a multidisciplinary expert group. Key areas covered include escalation of treatment for asthma exacerbations, maintenance therapy, clinical diagnosis of bronchiolitis, indications for hospital admission, and the use of oxygen therapy and other supportive interventions. It also addresses considerations for implementation, monitoring and future updates. Intended for policy-makers, programme managers and health care providers, it supports the delivery of consistent, high-quality care and contributes to efforts to reduce preventable child morbidity and mortality.

guideline_records.guideline_title: A Synopsis of the 2025 U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and U.S. Department of Defense Clinical Practice Guideline for the Primary Care Management of Asthma
guideline_records.scope: Primary care routine asthma evaluation and maintenance management
guideline_records.abstract: Description The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) updated the 2019 joint clinical practice guideline (CPG) for the primary care management of asthma. This synopsis provides primary care providers with a summary of the updated 2025 recommendations regarding evaluation and management of veterans and military members with asthma. Methods In 2024, the VA/DOD convened a guideline work group (WG), including clinical stakeholders, to update the joint VA/DOD guideline and conformed to the National Academy of Medicine's tenets for trustworthy CPGs. The WG drafted 12 key questions, reviewed systematically identified literature (20 July 2018 through 15 May 2024), evaluated the evidence, created algorithms, and advanced 21 evidence-based recommendations in accordance with the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) system. Recommendations The WG strongly recommended inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) and streamlined management of asthma by suggesting a combination of ICS and rapid-onset long-acting β-agonist as both reliever and controller agents and step-up therapy by increasing ICS and/or adding long-acting anticholinergic agents. The WG also supported the management of symptomatic gastroesophageal reflux disease and obesity for better control of asthma. The WG suggested against the use of indoor air filtration devices. Finally, the WG outlined decision points for referral to a subspecialist.

guideline_records.guideline_title: Allergic Rhinitis and Its Impact on Asthma (ARIA)-EAACI Guidelines-2024-2025 Revision: Part II-Guidelines on Oral and Ocular Treatments
guideline_records.scope: Clinical practice recommendations on asthma management
guideline_records.abstract: Background Oral and ocular medications are frequently used in the treatment of allergic rhinitis (AR). As part of the update of the Allergic Rhinitis and its Impact on Asthma (ARIA)-EAACI guidelines, this manuscript presents the ARIA-EAACI 2024-2025 recommendations for oral and ocular treatments. Methods The ARIA-EAACI 2024-2025 guideline panel issued recommendations following the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence-to-decision framework. Several sources of evidence were used to inform panel judgements and recommendations, including systematic reviews, mHealth and pharmacovigilance data as well as a survey on costs. Results Eight guideline questions concerning oral treatments for AR and three questions concerning ocular treatments were addressed. These questions led to the recommendations. Overall, these questions concern the choice between different classes of medication. They also discuss the role of oral antihistamines (OAH), leukotriene receptor antagonists (LTRA), ocular antihistamines (OcAH) and ocular mast cell stabilisers. Four questions had not been previously evaluated in ARIA guidelines, while, for the other four, there was a change in the strength or directionality of the recommendations. Overall, these guidelines recommend using intranasal corticosteroids over OAH and using OAH over LTRA. Moreover, they suggest using OAH over OcAH and suggest being against adding LTRA to OAH. Finally, considerations for choosing between different individual OAHs are presented. Conclusion This ARIA-EAACI 2024-2025 article supports patients, their caregivers and healthcare professionals in choosing oral and ocular treatments for AR. Decisions on treatment should consider the clinical variability of the disease, patients' values and the affordability of medications.

guideline_records.guideline_title: Severe Asthma in Children and Adolescents: an AWMF Guideline by the German Society for Pediatric Pulmonology
guideline_records.scope: Severe refractory asthma phenotyping, biologic selection, and exacerbation risk reduction
guideline_records.abstract: Asthma is the most common chronic respiratory disease in children and adolescents. While most patients achieve good control with guideline-based treatment, a significant proportion experience persistent symptoms, frequent exacerbations, and impaired quality of life.This guideline aims to define severe and difficult-to-treat asthma in children and adolescents, support diagnostic precision, and provide practical, evidence-based recommendations for assessment and management, including biological therapies.The S1 guideline was developed under the coordination of the German Society for Pediatric Pulmonology following AWMF procedures. A structured consensus process involving experts from pediatric pulmonology, allergology, and general pediatrics was conducted. Existing national and international guidelines and new evidence were systematically reviewed and adapted.Key elements include a stepwise diagnostic algorithm to distinguish difficult-to-treat from truly severe asthma, guidance on assessing adherence, comorbidities, and inflammation biomarkers, and recommendations for targeted biological treatment. This guideline addresses monitoring tools, transition to adult care, and the role of rehabilitation.Children and adolescents with severe asthma require early referral to specialized centers and a structured, interdisciplinary approach. Personalized treatment strategies-including biologics-should be guided by phenotyping and biomarkers. Registry data are essential to improve care quality and generate real-world evidence.

validated_clinical_rules.guideline_source: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report & BTS/SIGN
validated_clinical_rules.rule_summary: SABA (Salbutamol 4–10 puffs pMDI+spacer or 2.5–5mg neb every 20 min in 1st hour) + SAMA (Ipratropium 500mcg neb in moderate/severe) + Systemic Corticosteroid (Prednisolone 40–50mg/d PO x5d adult; 1–2 mg/kg/d max 40mg child).

numerical_parameters.saba_adult_dose: 4–10 puffs pMDI with spacer every 20 min for 1 hour, then 4–10 puffs every 1–4 hours
numerical_parameters.saba_pediatric_dose: 2–6 puffs pMDI with spacer every 20 min for 1 hour, then 2–4 puffs every 1–4 hours
numerical_parameters.systemic_steroid_adult: Prednisolone 40–50 mg orally once daily for 5 days (no taper needed)
numerical_parameters.systemic_steroid_child: Prednisolone 1–2 mg/kg/day (maximum 40 mg) orally for 3–5 days
numerical_parameters.magnesium_sulfate_adult: 2.0 g IV infusion in 100 ml 0.9% NaCl over 20 minutes (in severe refractory cases)
numerical_parameters.magnesium_sulfate_child: 50 mg/kg (maximum 2.0 g) IV infusion over 20 minutes

conditional_qualifications: Use pMDI with dedicated spacer in preference to nebulizers when possible to ensure superior lung deposition and avoid aerosol dispersion.
Oral corticosteroids are pharmacologically bioequivalent to IV hydrocortisone and should be preferred unless the patient is unable to swallow or vomiting.
contraindications: Do NOT use sedatives or anxiolytics in acute asthma exacerbations (respiratory depression risk).
Do NOT delay systemic corticosteroid administration in moderate-to-severe exacerbations.
